correctness.rationale: The Mallows partition function is the product of q-integers. Deletion of fixed boundary entries gives the one- and two-site probabilities. Splitting on the first image when the second is fixed gives the otherwise nontrivial second-site marginal with exponent k; subtraction yields the two exact signed covariances. A monotone threshold equation has one root, and controlled Taylor/Riemann-sum expansions prove both the cubic and quartic weak-bias limits. Packaged verifier independently enumerates 35 exact rational parameter-size cases, six identities per case (210 exact assertions). The proof covers all n≥3 and q>0; tests are not claimed as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural adjacent-versus-opposite boundary dependence comparison in a classical random-ranking model has an exact sign phase for every n and q, the first possible negative-dependence size, a decreasing critical sequence, and two orders of asymptotic crossover. The log 2 threshold cannot be inferred from the uniform covariance or aggregate Poisson law. It is a full classification of these motivated local dependence observables, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a routine positivity check.
